title: Relative regular equations remain regular locally after base change
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] of commutative rings with $A$ finitely presented over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $b\geq0$ and let $f_1,\ldots,f_b\in A$ be an $A$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and assume that $A/(f_1,\ldots,f_b)$ is flat over $R$. For any homomorphism $R\to R'$ of commutative rings, put $A'=A\otimes_RR'$ and $f'_j=f_j\otimes1$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(a\otimes r)(a_1\otimes r_1)=aa_1\otimes rr_1$ and unit $1\otimes1$. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak q'\subset A'$ containing all the $f'_j$, the elements $f'_1/1,\ldots,f'_b/1$ form a regular sequence in the local ring $A'_{\mathfrak q'}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

proof.text: Contract $q\subset A\otimes_RR'$ to $p\subset A$ and then to $r\subset R$. Put $S=A_p$, $R_l=R_r$, $k=\kappa(r)$ and $P=(R\setminus r)^{-1}A$. The natural map $R_l\to S$ is local. The tensor-localization pushout identifies $P$ with $R_l\otimes_RA$, so $P$ is finitely presented over $R_l$; $S$ is a further localization of $P$. Flatness of $A$ and $A/(f)$ is preserved by localization, and flatness over $R_l$ is equivalent to flatness over $R$ for these modules. Localize the original regular sequence to obtain the specified regular sequence $g$ in $S$.

Apply [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial] to $g$ in $S$, then [lem-pur-quasi-regular-flat-quotient-base-change] to $R\to k$; the final quotient is $R$-flat by step 1. This proves bijectivity of the canonical polynomial associated-graded map for $g\otimes1$ in $F=S\otimes_Rk$. Since $R_l$ is a localization, tensoring the two $R_l$-algebras $S,k$ over $R$ or $R_l$ gives the same algebra. Hence $F\cong S/(\mathfrak m_{R_l}S)$ is local. Also $F$ is a localization of $A\otimes_Rk$, which is finite type over the field $k$, hence Noetherian. All equations lie in its maximal ideal. Apply [lem-pur-quasi-regular-noetherian-local] to obtain regularity on this closed fibre.

Induct on the prefix length $i$ to prove that $Q_i=S/(g_0,\ldots,g_{i-1})$ is $R_l$-flat. At $i=0$ this is $S$. For the step, $Q_i$ is finitely presented as an $S$-module because its defining ideal is generated by a finite list. Its closed fibre identifies by the double-quotient interchange with the corresponding prefix quotient of the regular closed-fibre sequence of step 2. Thus multiplication by $g_i$ is injective on that closed fibre. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-general-mod-injective] to the essentially finitely presented local map $R_l\to S$, source and target both $Q_i$, and multiplication by $g_i$. Its cokernel is $Q_{i+1}$ by the iterated-quotient equivalence. This gives the next flatness assertion. Restricting scalars back to $R$ proves flatness of every prefix. The finite-presentation witness is the explicitly constructed $P$ of step 1.

Multiplication by $g_i$ on $Q_i$ is injective by localization of the original regular sequence. Its cokernel $Q_{i+1}$ is $R$-flat by step 3. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] with the arbitrary module $R'$, and flip tensor factors, to obtain injectivity of multiplication by $g_i$ on $Q_i\otimes_RR'$. The tensor-quotient equivalence sends $[s]\otimes t$ to $[s\otimes t]$ and identifies each tensor prefix with the corresponding prefix of $E=S\otimes_RR'$. Therefore the images of the equations form a weakly regular sequence in $E$.

The tensor-localization comparison makes $E$ a localization of $B=A\otimes_RR'$ at the image of $A\setminus p$. Every element of this multiplicative set is outside $q$, by the definition of $p$. Thus $B_q$ is a further localization of $E$, with the maps agreeing on every specified equation. Flatness of localization preserves weak regularity. All equations lie in the maximal ideal of $B_q$ by their membership in $q$, so the local regularity criterion gives regularity, including the nonzero final quotient. The same argument covers an empty list.
